# What the distributed package's tests need, and nothing else.
#
# Kept out of the two runtime lockfiles on purpose. Those build the environment shipped to
# every user, and a test runner has no business on somebody's machine because they wanted to
# run a model. Continuous integration installs this file on top of the runtime environment;
# nothing in the application reads it.
pytest==8.4.2

# numpy is not a test dependency. It is what protocol._to_bytes uses to get a tensor's raw
# bytes, and both runtime lockfiles already carry it because transformers does, so the shipped
# environment has always had it. It is named here because continuous integration installs
# torch on its own, and without numpy every tensor frame fails to encode. Declaring it stops
# that from looking like a fault in the wire format, which is what it looked like the first
# time. There is no numpy-free way to do this that is not thousands of times slower; the
# reasoning is written out at the function.
numpy
